messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated p99 latency for /v1/chat/completions across us-west & eu-west. firing: latency.chat.completions.p99 > 1200ms (5m)
alice: seeing a spike in queued tokens on the dedicated pool, p99 up to ~1800ms on m-std models :grimacing:
ben: confirmed. autoscaler didn't kick for one of the dedicated groups, looks like a config drift after yesterday's rollout.
carol: do we have customer impact? any 5xx or client retries? we should prioritize user-facing mitigation first.
dmitri: some customers reported slow responses and a couple of retries. CX logged two high-priority tickets for enterprise accounts.
sre-oncall: oncall here, I'm going to open quick mitigations: 1) scale up dedicated pool by +2 gpus, 2) route non-enterprise traffic to smaller model variant, 3) temporarily raise p99 alert threshold to 2s to reduce noise while we stabilize. any objections?
alice: +1 to scaling and route fallback. raising alert threshold is fine but let's record the change and add noise gating so we don't miss real degradation.
ben: low-risk config snippet to add to routing policy:
```
route: /v1/chat/completions
priority: enterprise
fallback_model: gpt-mini-quant
route_percentage: non-enterprise=30
```
carol: I'll spin up a short-lived dashboard panel in observability: p95/p99 per-model, inflight queue length, autoscaler events. can we also add a tag for the rollout that touched autoscaler config?
dmitri: request to post a public-facing status: note degraded performance for some chat workloads, we're mitigating and will update in 30m.
sre-oncall: doing the scale now.
incident-bot: action log: scale_dedicated_pool uid=scale-2487654321 by +2 gpus; routing change applied; alert_threshold change applied to latency.chat.completions.p99 = 2000ms; ticket created INC-248765 for postmortem.
alice: autoscaler logs show a rejected scale request at 12:14 UTC due to quota check, I'm investigating whether the quota alert suppressed autoscaler retries.
ben: if quota is the blocker we should fallback to cold-start policy for the pool so we can ignore autoscaler for immediate scale (short-lived).
sre-oncall: applied cold-start override for this incident.
carol: dashboard panels now up at https://console/obs/d/248765 — added per-model p95/p99 + inflight queue, annotated with the scale action.
dmitri: posting status update: "We are mitigating elevated latency for chat completions. We have scaled capacity and applied routing fallbacks. No data loss. Updates in 30m." :megaphone:
alice: after scale p99 dropped to ~950ms, inflight queue normalized. still seeing a tail on m-std at higher seq lengths.
ben: suggest lowering the new p99 temporary threshold to 1500ms now that scale shows improvement, to catch regressions sooner.
sre-oncall: lowered alert threshold to 1500ms and re-enabled normal alert cadence. leaving a 15m cooldown to avoid immediate flapping.
dmitri: thanks team. recommending a follow-up: 1) postmortem to identify autoscaler drift + quota handling, 2) add per-model alerting rather than global route p99, 3) create Canary job that validates autoscaler behavior after config changes.
carol: I'll create the dashboard ticket and a small runbook for route-level thresholds.
alice: logging additional context for postmortem: sequence-length distribution change from a customer A/B test caused more long queries; saved traces in S3 under telemetry/248765.
ben: putting a PR together to add per-model p95/p99 alerts with noise gating and a minimum sample size.
sre-oncall: handing off to night oncall @dmitri - I left notes in the incident ticket. if it reoccurs escalate to infra team.
dmitri: got it. monitoring edge cases, will wake the team if it regresses. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
